pr_title: Fix collection callbacks not terminating when abort is thrown:
pr_body:
Fix collection callbacks not terminating when abort is thrown:

- Across ActiveRecord framework, `throw(:abort)` is used to early
  terminate callbacks (when saving, deleting a record ...).
  This is however not the case when we try to add a record to
  an association; throwing an abort inside any of `before_add
  or `before_remove` result in a hard exception.

  This commit fix that and in the case a `abort` is thrown, the record won't either be added or removed from the collection.

  Fix #37273

@kamipo 
cc/ @rafaelfranca @casperisfine @etiennebarrie
pr_comments:
How about just catching `:abort`?

Probably callback things on association could be refactored, but to fix #37273, it seems too much change to me.

https://github.com/rails/rails/compare/fix-collection-association-callback

```diff
diff --git a/activerecord/lib/active_record/associations/collection_association.rb b/activerecord/lib/active_record/associations/collection_association.rb
index ca65cf6145..dfd1abce3a 100644
--- a/activerecord/lib/active_record/associations/collection_association.rb
+++ b/activerecord/lib/active_record/associations/collection_association.rb
@@ -389,7 +389,9 @@ def delete_or_destroy(records, method)
         end

         def remove_records(existing_records, records, method)
-          records.each { |record| callback(:before_remove, record) }
+          catch(:abort) do
+            records.each { |record| callback(:before_remove, record) }
+          end || return

           delete_records(existing_records, method) if existing_records.any?
           @target -= records
@@ -445,7 +447,9 @@ def concat_records(records, raise = false)
         end

         def replace_on_target(record, index, skip_callbacks)
-          callback(:before_add, record) unless skip_callbacks
+          catch(:abort) do
+            callback(:before_add, record)
+          end || return unless skip_callbacks

           set_inverse_instance(record)

```

Yeah you are right, to fix #37273 this is enough. I originally tried to fix the issue in the associations builders like Rafael mentioned but I had issues mostly because the callback method receives an argument which isn't standard with ActiveSupport callbacks. Anyway, I think we should go with your solution

issue_context.title: Halt callback execution raises exception in relational callbacks
issue_context.body:
### Steps to reproduce

It is not clear from the documentation if this is an expected behavior or a bug.
It is stated that the callback chain can be halted by throwing an `:abort` exception.
This works well for model self contained callbacks.
However this is not true for **relational callbacks**, e.g. `has many` or `has_and_belongs_to_many`. If I try to halt the execution in a `before_add` callback by throwing `:abort` the exception bubbles up all the way to the app. 

```ruby
require "bundler/inline"

gemfile(true) do
  source "https://rubygems.org"

  gem "rails", "5.1"
  gem "sqlite3", "1.3.13"
end

require "active_record"
require "minitest/autorun"
require "logger"

ActiveRecord::Base.establish_connection(adapter: "sqlite3", database: ":memory:")
ActiveRecord::Base.logger = Logger.new(STDOUT)

ActiveRecord::Schema.define do
  create_table :entities, force: true do |t|
    t.boolean :abort_self_save, default: false
  end

  create_table :items, force: true do |t|
  end

  create_table :groups, force: true do |t|
  end

  create_join_table :entities, :groups do |t|
     t.index [:group_id, :entity_id], unique: true
  end
end

class Entity < ActiveRecord::Base
  before_save :rollback_method, if: -> (x) { x.abort_self_save }
  has_many :items, before_add: :rollback_method
  has_and_belongs_to_many :groups, before_add: :rollback_method

  def rollback_method(entity = nil)
    throw(:abort)
  end
end

class Item < ActiveRecord::Base
  belongs_to :entity
end

class Group < ActiveRecord::Base
  has_and_belongs_to_many :entities
end

class BugTest < Minitest::Test
  def test_normal_saving
    entity = Entity.create
    assert_equal 1, Entity.count
  end

  def test_aborted_saving
    entity = Entity.create(abort_self_save: true)
    assert_equal 0, Entity.count
  end

  def test_has_many
    entity = Entity.create
    entity.items << Item.create
    assert_equal 0, entity.items.reload.count
  end

  def test_habtm
    entity = Entity.create
    entity.groups << Group.create
    assert_equal 0, entity.groups.reload.count
  end
end
```

### Expected behavior
When trying to halt the callback execution chain in a relational callback, I should be able to throw `:abort` and stop it.

### Actual behavior
I tried to halt the callback execution chain in a relational callback, by throwing `:abort` but an exception was raised.

### System configuration
**Rails version**: 5.1.0

**Ruby version**: 2.3.3

review_comments: I think the proper fix for this is at the `define_callback` methods in the association builders.
